author: Marilyn A. Dyrud, Oregon Institute of Technology; 36th ASEE/IEEE Frontiers in Education Conference (2006)
locator: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire section: insurance settlement and civil-suit figures, citing Von Drehle (2003) and Pence et al. (2003)
notes: Reports, citing David Von Drehle, Triangle: The Fire That Changed America (2003), that Harris and Blanck collected $200,000 in insurance and an insurance settlement nearly $65,000 in excess of the factory's worth (about $445 per victim), while the 1914 civil settlement paid each plaintiff family $75 per life lost. The rounded popular account ($60,000 excess, about $400 per victim) is the same figure rounded down; this record states the paper's ~$65,000 / ~$445 figures.

title: Fire! Three Case Studies in Ethics (Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire section)
